questions.question: How does Pavanamuktasana differ from Setu Bandhasana in terms of their / primary benefits?
questions.solution_html:
• • Pavanamuktasana brings the knees towards the chest and is commonly associated with relieving abdominal gas and
  • supporting digestion.
  • • Setu Bandhasana lifts the pelvis and chest and strengthens the back and gluteal muscles.
  • • Setu Bandhasana also gently opens the chest, while Pavanamuktasana focuses more on abdominal compression.
questions.final_answer: • Setu Bandhasana also gently opens the chest, while Pavanamuktasana focuses more on abdominal compression

questions.question: Explain the important precautions and contraindications to be considered while / performing inverted Asanas.
questions.solution_html:
• • Learn inverted Asanas under the guidance of a qualified Yoga instructor, particularly as a beginner.
  • • Warm up properly and enter and leave the posture slowly; avoid jerky movements.
  • • Do not force the neck or place excessive pressure on the head and cervical spine.
  • • People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma or other serious eye conditions, significant neck/spinal problems
  • or certain heart conditions should avoid some inversions unless medically cleared.
  • • During pregnancy, or after an injury or surgery, obtain individual clinical advice before attempting inversions.
  • • Stop immediately if pain, dizziness, breathlessness, visual disturbance or unusual discomfort occurs.
  • • Use suitable support and a non-slip surface; avoid practice when exhausted.
  • • Avoid competing with others or holding the posture longer than comfortable.
questions.final_answer: • Avoid competing with others or holding the posture longer than comfortable
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Develop a short Yoga-based programme that combines suitable Asanas and / Pranayama for reducing stress and promoting relaxation.
questions.solution_html:
• Develop a short Yoga-based programme that combines suitable Asanas and Pranayama for reducing stress and promoting
  • relaxation.
  • • Begin in a quiet place with comfortable sitting and natural breathing for 2 minutes.
  • • Do gentle neck and shoulder movements for about 2 minutes, without forcing the joints.
  • • Practise Tadasana for 1 minute, followed by gentle cat-cow movements for 2 minutes.
  • • Practise Balasana for about 2 minutes and a comfortable seated forward bend if appropriate.
  • • Perform slow diaphragmatic breathing or gentle alternate-nostril breathing for 3–4 minutes; do not force the breath or hold
  • it.
  • • Finish in Savasana for 3–5 minutes, consciously relaxing the muscles.
questions.final_answer: • Finish in Savasana for 3–5 minutes, consciously relaxing the muscles
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the effects of Yoga on cardiovascular and respiratory functions.
questions.solution_html:
• • Slow breathing and relaxation may reduce stress-related arousal and support a calmer heart rate.
  • • Regular, appropriate Yoga practice may support blood-pressure management as part of a healthy lifestyle; it does not
  • replace medical treatment.
  • • Postures and movement provide gentle physical activity and may support circulation and functional fitness.
  • • Pranayama develops awareness and control of inhalation and exhalation.
  • • Breathing exercises may support respiratory muscle control and breathing efficiency in some practitioners.
  • • Relaxation may reduce the feeling of breathlessness associated with anxiety in some situations.
questions.final_answer: • Relaxation may reduce the feeling of breathlessness associated with anxiety in some situations
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Develop a simple daily Yoga programme combining Asanas, Pranayama and / healthy lifestyle practices for improving energy and vitality.
questions.solution_html:
• Develop a simple daily Yoga programme combining Asanas, Pranayama and healthy lifestyle practices for improving
  • energy and vitality.
  • • Start with 2–3 minutes of quiet sitting and gentle warm-up movements.
  • • Practise Surya Namaskar at a comfortable pace, for example 3–6 rounds according to ability.
  • • Add suitable Asanas such as Tadasana, Trikonasana and Bhujangasana, avoiding pain or strain.
  • • Practise gentle Pranayama, such as slow diaphragmatic breathing or Nadi Shodhana without breath retention, for 3–5
  • minutes.
  • • Finish with Savasana or quiet relaxation for 3–5 minutes.
  • • Maintain a balanced diet, adequate hydration, sufficient sleep and regular physical activity.
questions.final_answer: • Maintain a balanced diet, adequate hydration, sufficient sleep and regular physical activity
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: A beginner is learning Pranayama for the first time. Explain the basic principles / that should be followed for safe and effective practice.
questions.solution_html:
• A beginner is learning Pranayama for the first time. Explain the basic principles that should be followed for safe and
  • effective practice.
  • • Learn from a qualified instructor and begin with simple breathing techniques.
  • • Choose a clean, quiet and well-ventilated place; sit comfortably with the spine naturally upright.
  • • Start with natural, slow and smooth breathing without straining.
  • • Do not force inhalation or exhalation, over-breathe or hold the breath as a beginner.
  • • Start with a short duration and increase gradually as comfort and control improve.
  • • Practise when comfortable, preferably not immediately after a heavy meal.
  • • Stop if dizziness, tingling, chest discomfort, anxiety or unusual breathlessness occurs and return to normal breathing.
  • • People with significant heart or respiratory conditions should seek clinical advice before starting.
  • • Regularity and comfort are more important than forceful or prolonged practice.
questions.final_answer: • Regularity and comfort are more important than forceful or prolonged practice
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the benefits of Savasana, Ananda Balasana and Sukhasana for / mental health and relaxation.
questions.solution_html:
• • Savasana allows the whole body to rest and may reduce perceived tension and support calm awareness of breathing.
  • • Ananda Balasana gently moves the hips and may help release tension around the hips and lower back when performed
  • comfortably.
  • • Sukhasana provides a stable seated position for mindful breathing or meditation.
  • • These postures can help a person pause, settle attention and reduce the sense of stress.
  • • Regular comfortable practice may support relaxation, emotional wellbeing and body awareness.
questions.final_answer: • Regular comfortable practice may support relaxation, emotional wellbeing and body awareness
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the important precautions and contraindications to be considered while / performing inverted Asanas.
questions.solution_html:
• • Learn inverted Asanas under the guidance of a qualified Yoga instructor, particularly as a beginner.
  • • Warm up properly and enter and leave the posture slowly; avoid jerky movements.
  • • Do not force the neck or place excessive pressure on the head and cervical spine.
  • • People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma or other serious eye conditions, significant neck/spinal problems
  • or certain heart conditions should avoid some inversions unless medically cleared.
  • • During pregnancy, or after an injury or surgery, obtain individual clinical advice before attempting inversions.
  • • Stop immediately if pain, dizziness, breathlessness, visual disturbance or unusual discomfort occurs.
  • • Use suitable support and a non-slip surface; avoid practice when exhausted.
  • • Avoid competing with others or holding the posture longer than comfortable.
questions.final_answer: • Avoid competing with others or holding the posture longer than comfortable
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Develop a short Yoga-based programme that combines suitable Asanas and / Pranayama for reducing stress and promoting relaxation.
questions.solution_html:
• Develop a short Yoga-based programme that combines suitable Asanas and Pranayama for reducing stress and promoting
  • relaxation.
  • • Begin in a quiet place with comfortable sitting and natural breathing for 2 minutes.
  • • Do gentle neck and shoulder movements for about 2 minutes, without forcing the joints.
  • • Practise Tadasana for 1 minute, followed by gentle cat-cow movements for 2 minutes.
  • • Practise Balasana for about 2 minutes and a comfortable seated forward bend if appropriate.
  • • Perform slow diaphragmatic breathing or gentle alternate-nostril breathing for 3–4 minutes; do not force the breath or hold
  • it.
  • • Finish in Savasana for 3–5 minutes, consciously relaxing the muscles.
questions.final_answer: • Finish in Savasana for 3–5 minutes, consciously relaxing the muscles

questions.question: Discuss the effects of Yoga on cardiovascular and respiratory functions.
questions.solution_html:
• • Slow breathing and relaxation may reduce stress-related arousal and support a calmer heart rate.
  • • Regular, appropriate Yoga practice may support blood-pressure management as part of a healthy lifestyle; it does not
  • replace medical treatment.
  • • Postures and movement provide gentle physical activity and may support circulation and functional fitness.
  • • Pranayama develops awareness and control of inhalation and exhalation.
  • • Breathing exercises may support respiratory muscle control and breathing efficiency in some practitioners.
  • • Relaxation may reduce the feeling of breathlessness associated with anxiety in some situations.
questions.final_answer: • Relaxation may reduce the feeling of breathlessness associated with anxiety in some situations

questions.question: Develop a simple daily Yoga programme combining Asanas, Pranayama and / healthy lifestyle practices for improving energy and vitality.
questions.solution_html:
• Develop a simple daily Yoga programme combining Asanas, Pranayama and healthy lifestyle practices for improving
  • energy and vitality.
  • • Start with 2–3 minutes of quiet sitting and gentle warm-up movements.
  • • Practise Surya Namaskar at a comfortable pace, for example 3–6 rounds according to ability.
  • • Add suitable Asanas such as Tadasana, Trikonasana and Bhujangasana, avoiding pain or strain.
  • • Practise gentle Pranayama, such as slow diaphragmatic breathing or Nadi Shodhana without breath retention, for 3–5
  • minutes.
  • • Finish with Savasana or quiet relaxation for 3–5 minutes.
  • • Maintain a balanced diet, adequate hydration, sufficient sleep and regular physical activity.
questions.final_answer: • Maintain a balanced diet, adequate hydration, sufficient sleep and regular physical activity

questions.question: A beginner is learning Pranayama for the first time. Explain the basic principles / that should be followed for safe and effective practice.
questions.solution_html:
• A beginner is learning Pranayama for the first time. Explain the basic principles that should be followed for safe and
  • effective practice.
  • • Learn from a qualified instructor and begin with simple breathing techniques.
  • • Choose a clean, quiet and well-ventilated place; sit comfortably with the spine naturally upright.
  • • Start with natural, slow and smooth breathing without straining.
  • • Do not force inhalation or exhalation, over-breathe or hold the breath as a beginner.
  • • Start with a short duration and increase gradually as comfort and control improve.
  • • Practise when comfortable, preferably not immediately after a heavy meal.
  • • Stop if dizziness, tingling, chest discomfort, anxiety or unusual breathlessness occurs and return to normal breathing.
  • • People with significant heart or respiratory conditions should seek clinical advice before starting.
  • • Regularity and comfort are more important than forceful or prolonged practice.
questions.final_answer: • Regularity and comfort are more important than forceful or prolonged practice
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the benefits of Savasana, Ananda Balasana and Sukhasana for / mental health and relaxation.
questions.solution_html:
• • Savasana allows the whole body to rest and may reduce perceived tension and support calm awareness of breathing.
  • • Ananda Balasana gently moves the hips and may help release tension around the hips and lower back when performed
  • comfortably.
  • • Sukhasana provides a stable seated position for mindful breathing or meditation.
  • • These postures can help a person pause, settle attention and reduce the sense of stress.
  • • Regular comfortable practice may support relaxation, emotional wellbeing and body awareness.
questions.final_answer: • Regular comfortable practice may support relaxation, emotional wellbeing and body awareness
